page: Vultr voc-s-24c-192gb-5760s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server powered by an AMD EPYC processor. It features 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 12 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, providing a 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, and includes 5760 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. No GPU hardware is present on this instance.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core and single-core CPU performance, placing in the top 25% in stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core tests. Memory performance is highly polarized: large-block uncached read and write operations achieve top-tier status in the top 10% category, while small-block cached read operations and overall Passmark memory scores fall within the average range. Cryptographic and vector execution capabilities are supported via hardware-accelerated AES, SHA_NI, and AVX instructions, though AVX-512 is not available.

From a resource density perspective, this server offers a highly qualitative balance of high-capacity local NVMe storage and substantial memory allocation per core. This profile is well-suited for memory-intensive and storage-heavy workloads such as relational databases, large-scale caching layers, data indexing, and enterprise web serving. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent execution times, making it a reliable choice for production environments requiring predictable performance without virtualization-induced steal time.
